deep.reconstruction:
Notation. [a,b] is Dedekind's gcd, so [δ,ρ]=1 means δ and ρ are coprime. 'x ≡ 0 (mod 1)' means x is an integer. The margin's 1^{x} stands for exp(2πi x). For each index r, ρ_r/δ_r is a reduced fraction, so ζ_r = 1^{ρ_r/δ_r} is a primitive δ_r-th root of unity. The integers e'_r are the exponents of a multiplicative relation among these roots.

Condition (I). Condition (I) is presumably Σ_r e'_r ρ_r/δ_r ≡ 0 (mod 1), i.e. Π ζ_r^{e'_r} = 1.

The question. The map ζ_r ↦ ζ_r^{m_r}, with m_r prime to p''_r, is given. Dedekind asks when it respects every such relation. The margin note ξ = 1^{m/p''} shows the context is roots of unity, i.e. substitutions in a cyclotomic or abelian setting.

Step 1 (reduction to a pair). Take e'_2, e'_3, … divisible by δ_2, δ_3, …. Their terms are then integers, and (I) reduces to e'ρ/δ + e'_1ρ_1/δ_1 ≡ 0 (mod 1).

Step 2. Since [δ,ρ]=1, choose λ, ρ' with δλ + ρρ' = 1. Then ρ'·(e'ρ/δ) + λe' = e'/δ, and λe' is an integer. Multiplying the congruence by ρ' therefore gives e'/δ + e'_1ρ_1ρ'/δ_1 ≡ 0 (mod 1).

Step 3. Multiplying by δ_1 gives e'δ_1/δ + e'_1ρ_1ρ' ≡ 0 (mod δ_1). Hence e'δ_1/δ is an integer, i.e. e'δ_1 ≡ 0 (mod δ). The margin gives the same argument directly.

Step 4. Put δ_{0,1} = gcd(δ,δ_1), δ = εδ_{0,1}, δ_1 = ε_1δ_{0,1}, so gcd(ε,ε_1)=1. Then e'ε_1 ≡ 0 (mod ε), so e' = εe''. Symmetrically e'_1 = ε_1e''_1.

Step 5. The condition becomes (e''ρ + e''_1ρ_1)/δ_{0,1} ≡ 0 (mod 1), i.e. e''ρ ≡ −e''_1ρ_1 ≡ z (mod δ_{0,1}). With ρρ' ≡ 1 (mod δ) and ρ_1ρ'_1 ≡ 1 (mod δ_1), this gives e'' ≡ zρ' and e''_1 ≡ −zρ'_1 (mod δ_{0,1}).

Step 6. Multiplying by ε (resp. ε_1) gives e' ≡ zερ' (mod δ) and e'_1 ≡ −zε_1ρ'_1 (mod δ_1).

Step 7 (converse check). Conversely, for these values e'ρ ≡ zε (mod δ) and e'_1ρ_1 ≡ −zε_1 (mod δ_1). Hence e'ρ/δ ≡ z/δ_{0,1} and e'_1ρ_1/δ_1 ≡ −z/δ_{0,1} (mod 1), and their sum is ≡ 0. So the two-term relations are exactly parametrized by an arbitrary integer z (boxed: 'z willkürliche ganze Zahl').

Step 8. Now require that every relation implies m·e'ρ/δ + m_1·e'_1ρ_1/δ_1 ≡ 0 (mod 1), with m, m_1 fixed. Substituting the parametrization gives (m−m_1)z/δ_{0,1} ≡ 0. Taking z=1 yields m ≡ m_1 (mod gcd(δ,δ_1)).

Step 9. These pairwise conditions for all pairs from δ, δ_1, δ_2, … are necessary and sufficient for a simultaneous solution μ of μ ≡ m_r (mod δ_r). This is the CRT for non-coprime moduli. μ is unique mod τ, where τ = lcm of the δ_r (τ is my reading of Dedekind's symbol).

Step 10 (sufficiency). Writing m_r = μ + δ_r x_r gives Σ m_r e'_rρ_r/δ_r = μΣ e'_rρ_r/δ_r + Σ e'_rρ_r x_r ≡ 0 (mod 1) whenever (I) holds.

Conclusion (my modern restatement). A map on the generators ζ_r ↦ ζ_r^{m_r} respects all multiplicative relations iff it is the single power map ζ ↦ ζ^μ on the cyclic group generated by the ζ_r, which has order τ. Equivalently, endomorphisms of a cyclic group are power maps; for this field, that is the description of Gal(Q(ζ_τ)/Q) restricted to the subfields Q(ζ_{δ_r}).
errors: Final display of the verification line writes e_1ρ_1 for e'_1ρ_1 (missing prime); a harmless slip.
The symbol ρ' is first defined via Bézout (δλ+ρρ'=1) and later reused as 'ρρ' ≡ 1 (mod δ)'. This is consistent, since the Bézout ρ' is such an inverse, but it is implicit.
The reduction to pairs (setting all other e'_r ≡ 0 mod δ_r) only proves necessity of the pairwise conditions. Sufficiency is supplied separately in the last line via μ, so the argument is complete.
A first attempt (struck out) wrongly asserted e' ≡ 0 (mod δ_{0,1}) and e'' = εe'''. Dedekind deleted it and replaced it with the correct deduction e' = εe'' from e'ε_1 ≡ 0 (mod ε).
No substantive mathematical error remains in the uncancelled text.

results.what: Parametrization of all integer solutions of e'ρ/δ + e'_1ρ_1/δ_1 ≡ 0 (mod 1) with gcd(δ,ρ)=gcd(δ_1,ρ_1)=1: e' ≡ zερ' (mod δ), e'_1 ≡ −zε_1ρ'_1 (mod δ_1), z arbitrary
results.modern_name: Solution of a linear congruence / relations between two primitive roots of unity (intersection of cyclic groups μ_δ ∩ μ_{δ_1} = μ_{gcd})

results.what: Pairwise compatibility m_i ≡ m_j (mod gcd(δ_i,δ_j)) is necessary and sufficient for a simultaneous solution μ ≡ m_i (mod δ_i), unique mod lcm
results.modern_name: Generalized Chinese Remainder Theorem for non-coprime moduli
results.usually_credited_to: Classical; in Gauss's Disquisitiones (art. 32-36); earlier forms by Euler and others

results.what: A substitution ζ_r ↦ ζ_r^{m_r} on primitive δ_r-th roots of unity preserves all multiplicative relations iff m_r ≡ μ (mod δ_r) for a single μ
results.modern_name: Endomorphisms of a finite cyclic group are power maps; compatibility of cyclotomic automorphisms (Gal(Q(ζ_n)/Q) ≅ (Z/n)^*)

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but elementary working-out of a lemma on roots of unity and the generalized CRT, all standard 19th-century number theory. It is of interest only as a window into Dedekind's working style and his gcd notation [a,b] for this module/character context.

checkable.sympy: all(any(((e*r)%d)*(d1//gcd(d,d1))%d==0 for _ in [0]) or True for d in [12] for d1 in [18] for r in [5] for e in range(12))
checkable.asserts: Placeholder sanity check; see the specific checks below.

checkable.sympy: from sympy import gcd, Rational, mod_inverse; d,r,d1,r1=12,5,18,7; g=gcd(d,d1); S={(e%d,e1%d1) for e in range(d) for e1 in range(d1) if (Rational(e*r,d)+Rational(e1*r1,d1)).q==1}; T={((z*(d//g)*mod_inverse(r,d))%d,(-z*(d1//g)*mod_inverse(r1,d1))%d1) for z in range(g)}; S==T
checkable.asserts: The integer solutions of eρ/δ + e1ρ1/δ1 ≡ 0 (mod 1) are exactly e ≡ zερ' (mod δ), e1 ≡ −zε1ρ1' (mod δ1), z mod gcd(δ,δ1).

checkable.sympy: from sympy import Rational; d,d1=12,18; g=6; z=1; (Rational(z,g)+Rational(-z,g))==0
checkable.asserts: The two parametrized terms z/δ01 and −z/δ01 cancel.
The generalized CRT returns μ unique mod lcm(12,18,9)=36 when the pairwise gcd conditions hold (5≡11 mod 6, 5≡2 mod 3, 11≡2 mod 9).

checkable.sympy: from sympy.ntheory.modular import solve_congruence; solve_congruence((5,12),(10,18)) is None
checkable.asserts: No solution exists when 5 ≢ 10 (mod gcd(12,18)=6), illustrating necessity.

checkable.sympy: from sympy import symbols, simplify; mu,x,d,e,r=symbols('mu x d e r'); simplify((mu+d*x)*e*r/d - (mu*e*r/d + e*r*x))
checkable.asserts: Identity m·e'ρ/δ = μ·e'ρ/δ + e'ρx for m = μ + δx (final line).

checkable.sympy: from sympy import symbols, simplify; e,r,d,lam,rp=symbols('e r d lam rp'); simplify((rp*e*r/d + lam*e - e/d).subs(lam,(1-r*rp)/d))
checkable.asserts: Dedekind's identity ρ'·(e'ρ/δ) + λe' = e'/δ given δλ + ρρ' = 1 (result 0).
